description: Behavioural corpus for every shipped bash-validator.sh (four editions plus Infrastructure-Creator, each through its .claude, .cursor and .codex copy and its host's payload shape). A case's expectation holds in the editions it lists ('all' = every one) and the opposite holds in the others. Run by tests/test_bash_validator_corpus.py.

decisions.--force-with-lease: Blocked. It still rewrites the remote branch; the lease only protects against overwriting commits the agent has not fetched. AGENTS.md forbids force-push without explicit user consent, and a hook cannot see consent, so the user runs it.
decisions.sandbox: The validator guards against accidental destruction; it is not a sandbox. A script written to disk and run later, or text piped into a shell, is not inspected.
decisions.delete-from: DELETE with no WHERE, and TRUNCATE without TABLE, are refused only when a simple command of the input runs SQL text (mysql, psql, sqlite3, wp db query, dbal:run-sql, artisan tinker, ...). Elsewhere 'delete from the cart' is a test name, an issue title or a translation. DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE TABLE and an always-true WHERE (1=1, true, bare 1) stay refused everywhere, as before.
decisions.core.hooksPath: Every git config write or unset of core.hooksPath is refused, also one that points the hooks at a project directory such as .githooks: the hook cannot tell enabling hooks from disabling them, so the user runs it.
decisions.launchers: A quoted command line is checked as a command only when a known launcher (BV_LAUNCHERS: ssh, ddev, lando, vagrant, docker, kubectl, tmux, ...) receives it; a quoted argument of any other program is text.
decisions.nesting: Nesting deeper than any real command (BV_MAX_NEST call frames) is refused as 'command too complex' instead of parsed: bash would overflow its stack and the hook would fail open.
